    FMOD Audio Source

    FMODAudioSource is a component that plays FMOD Events from a GameObject, much like Unity's AudioSource. You can use the same component for sounds that need continuous control, such as background music, as well as parameterized effects and 3D audio.

    This page walks through the complete workflow, from selecting and playing an Event to controlling it at runtime.

    Add the component

    Add FMODAudioSource in either of these ways:

    • Select GameObject > Audio > FMOD > Audio Source to create a new Audio Source GameObject.
    • On an existing GameObject, select FMOD Studio > FMOD Plus > FMOD Audio Source from Add Component.

    The Scene needs an FMOD Studio Listener for you to hear the sound. The Listener is usually added to the Main Camera.

    Select an Event

    Use Clip Style in the Inspector to choose how the Event is assigned.

    Select an Event directly

    Use the following setup when a GameObject always plays one specific Event:

    1. Set Clip Style to Event Reference.
    2. Select an FMOD Event in the Event field.

    Select from a Key List

    Set Clip Style to Key when multiple Audio Sources should share Events by name, or when you want to manage an Event and its initial Parameters together.

    1. For a Global Key, enable Use Global Key List and select AMB, BGM, or SFX.
    2. For a Scene or Prefab Key List, disable Use Global Key List and assign a LocalKeyList to Key List.
    3. Select the entry to play from Key.

    Changing Clip Style clears the previous selection, so select the Event or Key again. See Global and Local Key Lists to learn how to create Keys.

    Play a sound

    Play automatically when enabled

    To play as soon as the GameObject becomes enabled:

    1. Select an Event or Key.
    2. Enable Play On Awake.
    3. Enter Play Mode.

    Enabling the GameObject or component again requests playback again. When it is disabled, the sound stops according to Allow Fadeout When Stopping.

    Play from code or a UnityEvent

    To play at a specific time, such as from a button, Timeline, or game state, disable Play On Awake and call Play().

    using FMODPlus;
using UnityEngine;

public class MusicController : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource;

    public void PlayMusic()
    {
        audioSource.Play();
    }
}

    In a UnityEvent, select FMODAudioSource.Play() on the target GameObject to connect the same action without another script.

    Calling Play() does nothing when no Event is assigned.

    Control playback

    Choose how to stop

    Set Allow Fadeout When Stopping under Advanced Controls, then call Stop() to use that setting.

    public void StopMusic()
{
    audioSource.Stop();
}

    Use Stop(bool) when you need to choose the stop behavior for each call.

    // Use the fadeout authored in FMOD Studio.
audioSource.Stop(true);

// Stop the sound immediately.
audioSource.Stop(false);

    The actual fade curve and duration for Stop(true) must be authored on the Event in FMOD Studio. Without a fadeout or AHDSR release, it may sound similar to an immediate stop.

    Pause and resume

    Call Pause() to stop at the current playback position and UnPause() to continue from that position.

    public void PauseMusic()
{
    audioSource.Pause();
}

public void ResumeMusic()
{
    audioSource.UnPause();
}

    Mute playback

    Enable Mute in the Inspector or set mute to true to pause the current sound. Disable Mute or set it to false to continue playback.

    audioSource.mute = true;
audioSource.mute = false;

    Adjust Volume and Pitch

    Adjust the current sound's volume and playback rate in the Inspector or from code.

    audioSource.Volume = 0.5f;
audioSource.Pitch = 1.2f;
    • Volume is limited to the range from 0 to 1.
    • Pitch is limited to the range from -3 to 3.
    • Values set before playback are used the next time the Event plays.

    Change the Event at runtime

    To switch music or effects as the game progresses, assign a new EventReference to clip, then call Play().

    using FMODPlus;
using FMODUnity;
using UnityEngine;

public class StageMusic : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource;
    [SerializeField] private EventReference stageTwoMusic;

    public void ChangeToStageTwo()
    {
        audioSource.clip = stageTwoMusic;
        audioSource.Play();
    }
}

    Changing clip immediately clears the sound that was previously playing. The new Event does not start automatically, so call Play() when it should begin.

    Use Event Parameters

    Parameters let you change states such as a music stage, effect intensity, or surface type without replacing the Event.

    Apply initial values when playback starts

    After selecting an Event, Initial Parameter Values appears in the Inspector.

    1. Expand Initial Parameter Values.
    2. Select a Local Parameter from Add.
    3. Set the value to use when playback starts.

    The registered values are applied every time Play() starts the sound. When using a Key List, you can configure Parameters from the Event linked to the selected Key.

    Change a Parameter during playback

    Pass the Parameter name and value to SetParameter().

    public void ChangeStage(float value)
{
    audioSource.SetParameter("Stage", value);
}

    Pass true as the third argument to ignore the Seek Speed authored in FMOD Studio and apply the value immediately.

    audioSource.SetParameter("Stage", 1f, true);

    Apply multiple Parameters together

    Create an array of ParamRef values and pass it to ApplyParameter().

    audioSource.ApplyParameter(new[]
{
    new ParamRef { Name = "Stage", Value = 1f },
    new ParamRef { Name = "Intensity", Value = 0.75f },
});

    If a matching name is registered under Initial Parameter Values, the new value is also used for subsequent playback.

    Use a Parameter ID

    When changing a Parameter frequently, such as every frame, look up and store its FMOD PARAMETER_ID once instead of using its name each time.

    using FMOD.Studio;
using FMODUnity;

private PARAMETER_ID stageParameterId;
private bool hasStageParameter;

private void CacheStageParameter()
{
    EventDescription eventDescription = RuntimeManager.GetEventDescription(audioSource.clip);
    hasStageParameter = eventDescription.getParameterDescriptionByName(
        "Stage", out PARAMETER_DESCRIPTION description) == FMOD.RESULT.OK;

    if (hasStageParameter)
        stageParameterId = description.id;
}

public void ChangeStageFrequently(float value)
{
    if (hasStageParameter)
        audioSource.SetParameter(stageParameterId, value);
}

    Call CacheStageParameter() once after selecting or changing the Event, then use the stored ID through ChangeStageFrequently().

    Play short effects as one-shots

    One-shots are best for short sounds that can overlap, such as button clicks, impacts, and footsteps.

    Required behavior Method to use
    Repeat or overlap a short sound PlayOneShot()
    Stop, pause, or key off the sound later Set clip and use Play()
    Play the currently selected Event once at the current position PlayThisOneShot()

    Play an Event Reference or path

    using FMODPlus;
using FMODUnity;
using UnityEngine;

public class EffectPlayer : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private FMODAudioSource audioSource;
    [SerializeField] private EventReference hitEffect;

    public void PlayHit()
    {
        audioSource.PlayOneShot(hitEffect, 1f, transform.position);
    }

    public void PlayHitByPath()
    {
        audioSource.PlayOneShot("event:/SFX/Hit", 1f, transform.position);
    }
}

    When omitted, volumeScale defaults to 1 and position defaults to Vector3.zero. Pass transform.position or an impact point explicitly so a 3D effect plays at the intended location.

    You cannot later control a one-shot with this component's Stop(), Pause(), or KeyOff(). Use regular Play() when the sound needs control after it starts.

    Play with Parameters

    Pass a name and value directly for a single Parameter.

    audioSource.PlayOneShot(
    hitEffect,
    "Surface",
    2f,
    volumeScale: 1f,
    position: transform.position);

    Pass a collection of ParamRef values for multiple Parameters.

    var parameters = new[]
{
    new ParamRef { Name = "Surface", Value = 2f },
    new ParamRef { Name = "Intensity", Value = 0.5f },
};

audioSource.PlayOneShot(hitEffect, parameters, 1f, transform.position);

    Play the currently selected Event

    PlayThisOneShot() plays the current clip once at this GameObject's position and current Volume.

    audioSource.PlayThisOneShot();

    It does not automatically pass Initial Parameter Values. Use a PlayOneShot() overload that accepts Parameters when they are required.

    Continue past a sustain point

    When an FMOD Studio Event is authored to wait at a sustain point, call KeyOff() to continue to its next section.

    public void ContinueDialogue()
{
    audioSource.KeyOff();
}

    TriggerCue() sends the same command to the current Event.

    audioSource.TriggerCue();

    There is no audible change when the Event has no sustain point.

    Play 3D audio

    When you select an Event authored as 3D in FMOD Studio, its sound follows the GameObject containing FMODAudioSource.

    1. Configure the Event as 3D in FMOD Studio and rebuild the Bank.
    2. Select the Event on FMODAudioSource in Unity.
    3. Confirm that the Main Camera or player has an FMOD Studio Listener.
    4. Place or move the Audio Source GameObject at the desired position.

    Velocity is supplied according to how the GameObject moves:

    • When a Rigidbody or Rigidbody2D is present, its Velocity is used.
    • When moving the Transform directly without a Rigidbody, enable Non-Rigidbody Velocity if the sound needs Doppler.
    • Do not enable Non-Rigidbody Velocity when a Rigidbody is present.

    Change attenuation distances

    Enable Override Attenuation when only this Audio Source should use different attenuation distances from the FMOD Studio Event.

    • Min: the distance where attenuation begins
    • Max: the maximum attenuation distance

    Max cannot be less than Min. You can also adjust both distances with the radius handles in the Scene view. This setting is available only for 3D Events.

    Handle continuous Events outside the maximum distance

    When Stop Events Outside Max Distance is enabled in FMOD for Unity settings, a continuous 3D Event stops while the Listener is outside Max Distance and starts again from the beginning when it returns inside. Parameters changed during playback are applied again.

    A 3D one-shot uses the position supplied when it starts. Use regular Play() instead when the sound must keep following a moving object or needs to be stopped later.

    Control a Snapshot

    Select an FMOD Snapshot from the Event field, then use Play() and Stop() to enable and disable it like a regular Event.

    public void EnterCave()
{
    audioSource.Play();
}

public void ExitCave()
{
    audioSource.Stop();
}

    Use Event Trigger when a trigger volume or Unity Event should control the Snapshot.

    Options to use when needed

    Prepare the first playback

    For an Event that must start immediately after it is requested, enable Advanced Controls > Preload Sample Data. Preparing the selected Event's sample data ahead of time can reduce the first-play delay, but it may increase memory usage.

    Use it selectively for frequently used sounds that need an immediate response instead of enabling it for every Event.

    Allow playback only once

    Enable Trigger Once to ignore additional Play() requests after the current Event plays for the first time. Re-enabling the GameObject or calling Play() after Stop() does not play the same Event again.

    Assigning a different Event to clip at runtime allows that new Event to play once. Use this option for notifications or sequences that must occur only once.

    Check playback state and time

    Read the state properties to display playback progress in UI or prevent duplicate playback.

    if (!audioSource.isPlaying)
{
    audioSource.Play();
}

float duration = audioSource.Length;
float currentTime = audioSource.Time;
float progress = duration > 0f ? currentTime / duration : 0f;
    What to check Property
    Whether the current sound is playing or sustaining isPlaying
    Whether playback requested by Play() is still active IsActive
    Total duration of the selected Event in seconds Length
    Current playback position in seconds Time

    IsActive can remain true while a 3D Event is outside its maximum distance and currently inaudible. Use isPlaying when you need the actual playback state.

    Use EventInstance only when you need to call low-level FMOD functionality directly. Always check audioSource.EventInstance.isValid() first. Sounds played as one-shots cannot be controlled through this property.
